<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Proceeding to implement TicketStatus with a constructor that accepts a Set of allowed targets.

Using `Set.of` for immutable allowed targets. Adding `canTransitionTo` and `allowedTargets` methods.

Checking whether forward references to enum constants inside the constructor are safe in Java.

Realized Java enum constants may still be null during static initialization when referenced by earlier constants. This could break forward references in Set.of.

Confirmed the forward reference will likely trigger a compile error. Java does not allow referencing enum constants that appear later in the same enum declaration.

Evaluating workarounds for the forward reference issue. Considering a static initializer block or a static Map built after all enum constants exist. Also exploring an abstract method per enum constant as a classic pattern.

Anonymous subclasses resolve forward references lazily at runtime, so Set.of works safely there. Constructor references remain problematic. Java permits forward references in enum constructors, as shown by the Planet example.

Decided to use a static Map instead of constructor parameters. All enum constants are fully initialized when the static block runs, so forward references are safe.

Implemented the static Map ALLOWED mapping each status to its allowed transitions. Added canTransitionTo and allowedTargets methods. Confirmed Map.of produces immutable sets.

Will run the full Maven test suite including Testcontainers. Need to update the codebase map to mention TicketStatus. Checking prompt-history for formatting requirements.
</details></think>
